expectations.text: Distinguishes between possible CAUSES of the drop-off before proposing fixes, rather than going straight to an idea list
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'Four candidate causes' (never got it / got it and couldn't finish / got it and chose not to / shouldn't be counted) plus 'The cheapest test that splits all four' before any option is offered.

expectations.text: Raises that the 60% may be composed of different populations, or may be partly a measurement or attribution artifact
expectations.evidence: 'Some of them shouldn't be counted. Bots, duplicate signups, people who already have an account.' Also 'it's likely the 60% is several different failures stacked' and 'a suspicion abandon is invisible in your analytics because it looks identical to disinterest.'

expectations.text: Does not re-propose shortening the form or adding a progress bar
expectations.evidence: Explicitly excluded in the cut list: 'Shorter code, longer expiry, bigger button — same family as what you already tried. No screen-level change fixes a message that didn't arrive.'

expectations.text: At least one option questions whether verification needs to happen at that point in the flow at all
expectations.evidence: 'Bind the requirement to the action, not the account: Nothing needs proving at signup. Attach it to the first action that's costly to reverse.' Also 'Temporary identifier, reconciled afterwards' removes the gate entirely.

expectations.text: Options differ in mechanism (channel, timing, who verifies, whether to verify) rather than in copy, layout, or visual design
expectations.evidence: Five options map to five distinct mechanisms: occupy the idle wait (attention/timing), pre-commit sender identity (trust signalling), decouple identity resolution from service delivery (who/when verifies), move the gate to the risky action (whether/when to verify), treat abandonment as a resumable pause (recovery channel). No copy or layout item leads.

expectations.text: Handles the ambiguity in 'account-verification' — either asks which kind, or states which reading it assumed and what would change under the others
expectations.evidence: Line 3: 'I'm assuming this is an emailed link or a one-time code. If it's document KYC — ID upload, selfie — 60% is near industry-normal and the leverage moves to capture quality and retry handling instead.'

expectations.text: Proportionate to a bounded product question: under roughly 1200 words, no ceremonial section headings with no content under them
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 990 words, under the 1200 bar. Every heading carries content; the two structural blocks ('Cut, and why', 'What would change my ranking') are populated with substantive items.
